eyebrow: Paper entry · FARM clause choice · 2026-11-22, learning section 2026-11-24
title: Two right answers: the wording picks, not chance
subtitle: Some task cards accept more than one set of rules. We looked at which one the generator writes. Runs of one wording write the same answer, ordered tasks get the form the prompt teaches, and the card's first-listed answer gets no extra pull. Rewording the task is what moves the pick.

items: **Not random.** One wording gives one answer: 51 of 52 three-run groups agree, where a coin flip among the listed answers would make 27% agree.
**No pull toward `expect`.** It wins 84 of 153 right level runs, 55% [47%, 63%], against 50% for a uniform pick.

**Ordered tasks get the prompt's form.** The prompt teaches the last step's `Existence` plus the `Precedence`s. That form wins 12 of 12 final-run bundles and 119 of 119 level runs from low to max, whichever side the card lists it on.

**Rewording moves the pick, thinking does not.** On each of the 5 wording cards with four wordings, one or more wordings took the other answer: 8 of the 24 wording-card bundles, one run each. Low, medium, high and max pick the same on every right run.
**Pricing barely enters.** The generator never sees rewards. The critic does, and once moved a pick partly over reward (`tpl-precedence-soft-1-goal~p2`).

**Learning follows the level, not the answer.** Of the 9 trained rows on these cards, 5 of 5 learned on other levels and 0 of 4 on BlockedUnlockPickup; the answer the RM matched splits them 4 of 6 (later-listed) and 1 of 3 (first-listed). Three caveats below.

blocks.alt: Bars with 95% Wilson intervals: groups of runs that agree, the prompt's order form against expect, and the share of expect, with chance as diamonds.
blocks.caption: Runs of one wording repeat their answer far above chance, the prompt's order form wins on ordered tasks, and the share of `expect` stays at chance. Bars: share with its 95% Wilson interval; diamonds: the share a uniform pick among the card's listed answers would give. Made 2026-11-22 from `evidence/tables.md`.

items: **Two sets, never mixed.** (1) The final-run FARM bundles (freeze `809dfe3`, max thinking, generator deepseek-v4.1-flash, critic glm-5.3-flash): 36 bundles of 15 card entries that list more than one answer. (2) The thinking-level benchmark at the freeze (`docs/paper/level-benchmark-freeze/`): 11 of its 46 cases are such cards, 3 runs at each of 5 levels, 165 runs.

**Matching follows the repo scorer.** `clause_status` (`app/src/benchmark/rm_facts.py:133`) decides right or wrong; the script only names which answer it accepted: `expect`, then each `also_ok`, then the MONA same-task check. All 189 right answers matched exactly. A run the scorer rejects, or a failed run, is X (12, all at none or low).

**The prompt's form is a hand reading** of the generator prompt's order rules (`app/src/prompts/compiler-rm/reward-ltlf-creator.system.md:31-36, 41, 62-63`), one answer per ordered card (`PROMPT_FORM` in `check/clause_choice.py`).
**Chance** gives each right answer a uniform pick among the card's listed answers (1/2, or 1/3 for `tpl-not-co-existence-1-goal`); the tables add two-sided binomial p values.

blocks.text: **Ordered tasks: the prompt's form against `expect`**

The one miss: S1 at none, run 3, wrote the soft order the card lists as `expect`. Cards list the prompt's form as `expect` on 2 ordered cards and as `also_ok` on 7, so the `expect` share there only says which side the card author put it on.

**Pricing.** The generator prompt says "Do not output formulas, rewards" (`reward-ltlf-creator.system.md:89`). The critic sees the priced machine but is told not to judge reward magnitudes (`reward-machine-critic.system.md:17-20`). It switched one pick between listed answers, `tpl-precedence-soft-1-goal~p2` from E to A, because the commanded move "needs its own Existence" and the soft order alone "gives no reward for moving the ball". The data has no price variation to test more.

blocks.title: Six alternatives came from these bundles
blocks.text: On 2026-11-22 the user accepted the readings of 8 final-run bundles and added six new answers to six cards (`docs/paper/wrong-clauses-at-max/`). Those cards entered this set because a wording disagreed, so the final run overstates how often wordings split: its `expect` share is 24/36 with them and 11/15 without. The level benchmark ran before the ruling; only W2a (`tpl-precedence-1-nogoal`) is such a card there, and it never took the added answer.

blocks.title: Each reworded bundle ran once
blocks.text: Whether the 8 alternative wordings repeat their pick is not checked: one run each. Three reruns of those 8 wordings at max (24 model calls) would tell the wording from chance. The pattern below is a reading of 8 single runs, not a tested rule.

**What the alternative wordings share.** "Try to <do x> before y" got an extra soft `F x` on 4 of 4 action wordings (one through the critic); the one stated as a state ("preferably the ball is out of the way") did not. A "not both" split into two bans when the second half reads as its own act ("... and open the door in the same run") or when "both" sits on a list of places ("through both the top lane and the side lanes").
The script counts only final clauses. The critic rejected a first answer in 1 of 36 bundles and 7 of 165 level runs; none of those 7 switched between two listed answers (checked by hand).

sections.title: Learning follows the level, not the answer
sections.intro: The 9 trained rows of the cards above that list more than one answer (the final run, FARM, PPO). A row is learned when at least 2 of its seeds pass at 0.8 judged success (the final results' rule). E = `expect`, A = `also_ok[0]`; "added after" marks an answer listed only after the RMs were read. The answer is the one `check/clause_choice.py` matched for the bundle the runs trained on. Each card's task, its answers in LTLf and the machines the runs wrote are in the fold-out named in the last column, below.

blocks.text: **By level.** On other levels 5 of 5 rows learned; on BlockedUnlockPickup 0 of 4 did (Fisher's exact p = 0.008). **By answer.** 4 of the 6 rows whose RM matched a later-listed answer learned, 1 of the 3 that matched the first-listed one (p = 0.52): no pattern.

blocks.title: One learned row rests on the idle agent
blocks.text: `templates/tpl-not-co-existence-soft-1-nogoal` (soft not-both, no goal) has only soft rules, so its verdict compares the agents' soft-rule breaks with an idle plan's instead of a goal (`docs/paper/soft-breaks-vs-idle/`). Without it the split is 4 of 4 against 0 of 4, p = 0.029.

blocks.title: The study is not independent
blocks.text: 6 of the 15 cards (4 of them trained) got an accepted answer only after their RMs were read (see Gaps); 3 of the 9 rows match one of those answers (marked in the table).

blocks.title: Only 9 of the 60 trained rows
blocks.text: The other 51 trained rows are outside the study: their cards list one answer. The statement holds for these rows only.

blocks.title: A pattern over nine rows, not a cause
blocks.text: Across all 60 rows FARM learned 3 of 10 on BlockedUnlockPickup, so the level does not block learning by itself. For the 4 not-learned rows, ARM-FM learned 4 of them and no-RM 0. The level is also tangled with the code the runs trained on (`config.yaml` `git_head`): the not-learned rows on `029d82c` (2), `e6c3acb` (2), the learned rows on `809dfe3` (4), `e6c3acb` (1). `app/` is the same at `809dfe3` and `e6c3acb`; `029d82c` differs only in `app/src/benchmark/plan_check.py` and `traces.py` (`git diff --stat`; the runs' trees were marked dirty, so this is the commit, not the exact files). The runs do not say which part of the level or the machine stops FARM there.
